finding.problem: The change says each confirmation keeps the owner's reason, but only confirm_element takes and stores one. confirm_all_proposed confirms every proposed element through the same kernel confirm_element call with no reason, and confirm_wording_element does the same for an agent. Elements confirmed either way end up confirmed with confirmation_reason unset, so the note is missing exactly where later readers would look for it. The field is optional and nothing requires it on a confirmed element, so nothing flags the gap.
finding.where: authoring.domain.yaml: actions confirm_all_proposed and confirm_wording_element; objects.Element.confirmation_reason

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: confirm_all_proposed and confirm_wording_element confirm elements without a reason, so some confirmations lack the note; this is a real gap though not a seeded problem.

finding.problem: confirm_element now has a new required param (reason), so every existing caller that invokes it without one is broken. The domain's version stays at 4, and the composition still pins authoring interface 1, so consumers are given no signal that the action signature changed.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: Adding a required reason param to confirm_element changes its signature and breaks existing callers, with no version or interface bump.

finding.problem: The new reason param has no check that it is non-empty, so an owner can confirm with a blank string. The note is then recorded but says nothing about why the element was accepted, which defeats the purpose of the change.

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: The request does not ask for non-empty validation; this is speculative and not a defect in the change.

edit.why: It adds a confirmation_reason field on Element and a reason param on confirm_element that sets it, which is what the request asked for.
